TRANSPORTATION AND PUBLIC SAFETY COMMISSION
  TEMPLE CITY, CALIFORNIA

  REGULAR MEETING
  JUNE 24, 2026 - 7:00 P.M.
  COUNCIL CHAMBERS– 5938 KAUFFMAN AVE

  AGENDA

PROCEDURE TO ADDRESS TRANSPORTATION AND PUBLIC SAFETY COMMISSION: If
you wish to address the Transportation and Public Safety Commission, please complete a
speaker request form, indicating the agenda item number and submit it to the Clerk. There will
be a 3-minute time limit on each speaker, unless waived by the Commission. You have the
opportunity to address the Commission at the following times:

  •  AGENDA ITEM: at the time the Commission considers the agenda item.

  •  NON-AGENDA ITEM: at the time for PUBLIC COMMENTS. Please note that while
  the Commission values your comments, pursuant to the Brown Act, the Commission
  cannot take action on any item not listed on the agenda.

The listing of any items on the agenda includes the authority of the Commission to take action
on such item and to approve, disapprove, or give direction on any item.

  1.  CALL TO ORDER – Chairman Nimri

  2.  ROLL CALL – Commissioner Catalan, Lo, Xu, Stoll, Nimri

  3.  PLEDGE OF ALLEGIANCE

  4.  CEREMONIAL MATTERS

  A. REORGANIZATION OF COMMISSION

  The Commission will proceed with the annual reorganization of the
  Commission in appointing the Chairman and Vice-Chairman for a one-year
  term.

  5.  PUBLIC COMMENTS ON ITEMS NOT LISTED ON THE AGENDA

  The Transportation and Public Safety Commission will now hear public
  comments regarding items not listed on the agenda. The procedure to address
  the Commission is highlighted on the first page of this agenda.

  6.  CONSENT CALENDAR

  All Consent Calendar items may be approved in a single motion as
  recommended unless removed for further discussion. If members of the
  Commission or persons in the audience wish to discuss any matters listed on
  the Consent Calendar, please address them at this time.

7.  PARKING CITATION HEARINGS

  Please note that the hearing is an informal proceeding and the rules of evidence
  required in a court trial do not apply.

  Hearing Procedures:

  1.  When your case is called, approach the podium and state your name
  for the record.
  2.  State whether or not you are the registered owner of the vehicle cited.
  If you are not the owner, please state your relationship to the owner.
  3.  Present your case to the Commission. If you are submitting any
  documents or photographs relevant to your case, they will be retained
  by the City as part of the official file.
  4.  The Commission will render a decision to uphold or dismiss your
  citation. A written notification of the Commission’s decision will be
  mailed to you.
  5.  If your citation is upheld, you may appeal the decision of the
  Commission to the Los Angeles Superior Court – Stanley Mosk
  Courthouse. You must file your appeal within 30 days from the date
  the written notification is mailed to you.

  A. HEARINGS IN PERSON – None

  B. WRITTEN DECLARATION - None

8.  UNFINISHED BUSINESS – None

9.  NEW BUSINESS

  A. REVIEW THE ENGINEERING RECOMMENDATIONS FOR THE
  INTERSECTIONS OF SERENO DRIVE AND SULTANA AVENUE,
  (LOCATION 1), AND PENTLAND STREET AND SULTANA AVENUE,
  (LOCATION 2), AND THE NEED FOR ALL WAY STOP CONTROL AT THE
  INTERSECTIONS.

  PRESENTER:  Brian Cervantes, Transtech Engineers

  The Transportation and Public Safety Commission is requested to review
  resolution number 26-0001 and approve or deny the recommendations.

  Location 1: Sereno Drive at Sultana Avenue
  After a thorough review of existing traffic conditions and per the California
  Manual on Uniform Traffic Control Devices (CAMUTCD), California Vehicle
  Code (CVC), based on the traffic review and engineering judgement, it was
  found that the intersection of Sereno Drive and Sultana Avenue does not
  qualify for the installation of All-Way Stop Control. Neither of the streets met
  the minimum traffic volumes required to meet warrants.

  Recommendation:
  1. Install “Cross Traffic Does Not Stop” (W4 – 4P) Plaque underneath the
  Stop Sign located on the east side of Sultana Avenue, at the intersection
  with Sereno Drive.

  2. Install red reflective strip on the existing Stop Sign Signpost, that is
  located on the east side of Sultana Avenue, at the intersection with
  Sereno Drive.

  Location 2: Pentland Street at Sultana Avenue
  After a thorough review of existing traffic conditions and per the California
  Manual on Uniform Traffic Control Devices (CAMUTCD), California Vehicle
  Code (CVC), based on the traffic review and engineering judgement, it was
  found that the intersection of Pentland Street and Sultana Avenue does not
  qualify for the installation of All-Way Stop Control. The data collected along
  both streets showed significantly low traffic volumes. Neither street met the
  minimum traffic volumes required to meet warrants.

  Recommendation:

  1. Install “Cross Traffic Does Not Stop” Plaque (W4 – 4P) underneath the
  Stop Sign located on the south side of Pentland Street, at the intersection
  with Sultana Avenue.

  2. Install red reflective strip on the existing Stop Sign Signpost, located on
  the south side of Pentland Street, at the intersection with Sultana
  Avenue.

  3. Install 20 ft of red curb along the west side of Sultana Avenue, north of
  Pentland Street. This would push parked vehicles further from the
  intersection to improve line of sight for exiting vehicles on Pentland
  Street.

  B. REVIEW AND DISCUSS THE FINDINGS AND RECOMMENDATIONS OF
  THE TRAFFIC ENGINEERING REPORT CONCERNING THE PROPOSED
  INSTALLATION OF SPEED HUMPS FOR THE 6100 BLOCK OF CAMELLIA
  AVENUE NORTH OF GARIBALDI AVENUE.

  PRESENTER:  Brian Cervantes, Transtech Engineers

  The Transportation and Public Safety Commission is requested to review
  resolution number 26-0002 and approve or deny the recommendations.

  After a thorough review of existing traffic conditions and per the California
  Manual on Uniform Traffic Control Devices (CAMUTCD), California Vehicle
  Code (CVC), based on the traffic review and engineering judgement, this
  segment of Camellia Avenue, north of Garibaldi Avenue does not qualify for
  the installation of speed humps. The speed survey taken along the segment
  recorded the 85th% speed to be 23 MPH, which is 2 MPH below the prima
  facie speed limit along the residential Street. The data recorded do not
  reflect significant speeding issues. Additionally, this segment of Camellia
  Avenue extends from Garibaldi Avenue and ends in a Cul-de-Sac,
  approximately 820ft to the north. The segment only serves a limited number
  of households. According to the data recorded, the Average Daily Traffic was
  found to be 353 vehicles, 175 vehicles traveling northbound and 178
  vehicles traveling southbound.

  Recommendation:
  1. Install Speed Limit Signage (R2 – 1) on the east side of Camellia Avenue,
  approximately 65ft north of Garibaldi Avenue, for northbound traffic.
  Install “25” Pavement Legends along the northbound direction of
  Camellia Avenue, adjacent to the proposed sign.

  2. Install double yellow centerline along Camellia Avenue, from Garibaldi
  Avenue to the end of the Cul-de-Sac, to visually narrow the road.

  C. REVIEW THE RECOMMENDATION OF THE TRAFFIC ENGINEERING
  REPORT TO INSTALL AN ADDITIONAL 13 FEET OF RED CURB ON THE
  NORTHWEST SIDE OF SANTA ANITA AVENUE, RESULTING IN A TOTAL
  OF 31 FEET OF RED CURB NORTH OF THE INTERSECTION OF SANTA
  ANITA AVENUE AND GRAND AVENUE, WHILE RETAINING 20 FEET OF
  AVAILABLE CURB FOR PARKING, AND APPROVE OR DENY THE
  RECOMMENDATION.

  PRESENTER:  Brian Cervantes, Transtech Engineers

  The Transportation and Public Safety Commission is requested to review
  resolution number 26-0003 and approve or deny the recommendation.

  After a thorough review of existing traffic conditions and per the California
  Manual on Uniform Traffic Control Devices (CAMUTCD), California Vehicle
  Code (CVC), based on the traffic review and engineering judgement, it was
  determined that the intersection at Santa Anita Avenue and Grand Avenue
  would benefit from the installation of additional red curb at the northwest
  corner of the intersection. Based on the line-of-sight review completed at the
  intersection, drivers at the west leg turning onto Santa Anita Avenue from
  Grand Avenue have an unobstructed view of southbound traffic. However,
  visibility may be limited if large vehicles park closer to the intersection. It is
  recommended that the red curb be extended to ensure line-of-sight. The
  additional red curb would also be placed adjacent to an existing fire hydrant,
  where a minimum of 15-feet of red curb would be needed for emergency
  access, per (CVC SECTION 22514).

  Recommendation:
  1. Install an additional 13-feet of red curb on the northwest side of Santa
  Anita Avenue, for a total of 31-feet of red curb north of the intersection at
  Santa Anita Avenue and Grand Avenue leaving 20-feet of available curb
  for parking.

  D. REVIEW THE RECOMMENDATION OF THE TRAFFIC ENGINEERING
  REPORT FOR THE SHOPPING PLAZA DRIVEWAY AT, 5439 ROSEMEAD
  BOULEVARD, ON BROADWAY WEST OF ROSEMEAD BOULEVARD AND
  APPROVE OR DENY THE RECOMMENDATION TO ADD 20 FEET OF
  RED CURB ON THE SOUTH SIDE OF BROADWAY WEST OF THE
  SHOPPING CENTER DRIVEWAY.

  PRESENTER:  Brian Cervantes, Transtech Engineers

  The Transportation and Public Safety Commission is requested to review
  resolution number 26-0004 and approve or deny the recommendation.

  After a thorough review of existing traffic conditions and per the California
  Manual on Uniform Traffic Control Devices (CAMUTCD), California Vehicle
  Code (CVC), based on the traffic review and engineering judgement, it was
  concluded that this location would benefit from red curb at the shopping
  center driveway entrance/exit to improve line of sight.

  Recommendation:
  1.  Install 20-ft of red curb on the south side of Broadway, west of the
  shopping center driveway, located at 5439 Rosemead Boulevard. This
  change would remove approximately one parking space and leave
  approximately 29-ft of available parking space.
